content:
Rohit: Quick sync — proposal to add a tiny permission-eval service that returns a signed decision + optional pushdown filters. Goal is to centralize policy and produce stable cache tokens for our dashboard tile layer.

Lina: Why a service instead of a shared library? Concerned about the extra hop for every panel.

Rohit: Main reasons: single source of truth for policy, easier audit/tracing, and consistent key generation for caching across frontends. We can co-locate the service with query workers to minimize RTT.

Pedro: Co-location helps, but we need strict SLOs. Panels usually budget ~50ms p95. Any additional 5-10ms matters. Can we make common boolean checks inline and delegate only heavy filter materialization to the service?

Maya: Suggestion: service returns three fields: {allowed:boolean, cache_token:string (HMAC), stable_filters:[]}. UI/query layer uses stable_filters only when hint.stable=true. Otherwise apply post-filter.

Lina: How do we avoid blowing up tile keys if stable_filters vary?

Rohit: We'll only mark a filter stable if it maps to a canonical partition dimension (tenant_id, workspace_id). Dynamic attributes (role-scoped flags) remain ephemeral and won't be baked into tile keys.

Pedro: Invalidation model? If an admin revokes access, caches must reflect that fast. Event-driven invalidation + short TTL seems reasonable. What's the TTL?

Maya: Propose TTL=20s for cache_token, and we emit a role-version header that increments on writes. Query layer rejects tokens with stale version. Invalidation process: write -> bump role-version -> publish event -> invalidate local caches.

Lina: That implies eventual consistency window of ~20s + event fanout. Ops must accept that. For compliance-sensitive views we can force sync re-eval.

Pedro: Implementation sketch: gRPC endpoint EvaluatePermission(ctx, req) -> (allowed, token, filters, hint). Token = base64(hmac(user|view|version|expiry)). Workers keep small LRU of decode results.

Rohit: Observability: measure evaluation latency distribution, token cache hit rate, invalidation lag, and proportion of requests using baked vs post filters. We'll add these to the console perf dashboard.

Maya: Rollout plan: feature-flag per view + progressive enablement. Start with internal-only dashboards, then low-traffic public ones. Canary criteria: p95 panel latency delta < +7ms and no increased error budget for 30m.

Lina: Security: audit events must capture eval results for admin actions. Ensure logs redact PII. Tokens must be HMACed with rotating keys in KMS.

Pedro: One more: tile-cache fragmentation metric. If we see unique tile keys increase by >5% we should pause rollout.

deploy-bot: deploy.status: staging/perm-eval v0.1 deployed (build 1298). Metrics collector started. :white_check_mark:

Rohit: Next steps: I'll write a short RFC (API + invalidation semantics + rollout checklist). Please comment on the draft when I share.

Lina: +1 to RFC. Will add notes about co-locating with query workers and fallback logic.

Pedro: +1, will prototype token verification in the tile service and run microbenchmarks.

Maya: +1, will draft the canary dashboard and the fragmentation alert rules.

deploy-bot: reminder: collect logs for 24h post-deploy (job 1298).
